insights.title: Buybacks give way to organic deployment
insights.summary: Share repurchases fell from $8.32B in FY2026 Q1 (M19) to $6.79B in Q2 (M18) and $1.11B in Q3 (M17). Management moved its stated priority to investing in client franchises and organic growth, and in the Q3 call it described buybacks as coming after the dividend and organic investment.
insights.uw_relevance: Capital is being framed as retained for investment and possible deals rather than returned, which changes the capital and shareholder-return profile an underwriter would review. Management also referred to about $30 billion of excess capital in the Q3 call.

evidence.snippet: After you pay your dividend, which hopefully will be steady, we really like investing in organic growth.
evidence.source_title: JPMORGAN CHASE & CO earnings call 2026Q3 (quarter ended 2026-09-30)

evidence.snippet: as net income was more than offset by capital distributions and higher RWA.
evidence.source_title: JPMORGAN CHASE & CO earnings call 2026Q1 (quarter ended 2026-03-31)

insights.title: Underwriting standards loosening across leveraged credit
insights.summary: The Q1 2026 call first raised weakening underwriting, linked to private credit. The Q2 call listed specific weak terms such as weaker covenants and more rollover risk, while calling the deterioration mild. The Q3 call said credit terms had become a little loose and that management was tightening.
insights.uw_relevance: Loosening terms in leveraged and private credit are a credit-quality risk that is not yet visible in the reported ratios. The allowance-to-loans ratio stayed at 1.8% across FY2026 Q1 to Q3 (M87 to M89), so underwriters would need to weigh the qualitative commentary against those figures.

evidence.snippet: I pointed out that there has been some weakening in underwriting, not just by private credit.
evidence.source_title: JPMORGAN CHASE & CO earnings call 2026Q1 (quarter ended 2026-03-31)

evidence.snippet: Some weaker covenants, some people taking more rollover risk.
evidence.source_title: JPMORGAN CHASE & CO earnings call 2026Q2 (quarter ended 2026-06-30)

evidence.snippet: I think some of the credit terms have gotten a little bit loose.
evidence.source_title: JPMORGAN CHASE & CO earnings call 2026Q3 (quarter ended 2026-09-30)

insights.title: Investment banking outlook cools from healthy to slowed
insights.summary: The Q1 2026 call described client engagement and pipelines as healthy, with IB fees up 28% year on year. The Q2 call expected activity to remain healthy, with IB fees up 30%. In the Q3 call, management said evolving market conditions had recently slowed activity, and IB fees were up 14%.
insights.uw_relevance: Fee income in CIB is the most cyclical part of the revenue mix, and total revenue growth went from 27.7% YoY in FY2026 Q2 (M147) to 8.1% in Q3 (M146). Underwriters would watch whether the pipeline slowdown carries into the next quarter.

evidence.snippet: Looking ahead, client engagement and pipelines remain healthy, but of course, developments in the Middle East could have an impact on deal execution and timing.
evidence.source_title: JPMORGAN CHASE & CO earnings call 2026Q1 (quarter ended 2026-03-31)

insights.title: Consumer deposit outlook narrows and turns cautious
insights.summary: The Q1 2026 call expected low to mid-single-digit consumer deposit growth. The Q2 call narrowed this to low single-digit growth. The Q3 call reported consumer deposit growth of 4% year on year, but said higher rates could bring additional outflow pressure and weaker growth.
insights.uw_relevance: Deposits are the funding base, and total deposits rose from $2,713.70B in FY2026 Q2 (M48) to $2,780.79B in Q3 (M47). A shift toward rate-driven outflows would affect funding mix, so underwriters would track the uninsured share of deposits (64.0% in Q3, M179).

evidence.snippet: At Company Update we said we expect consumer deposit growth to be low to mid-single digits, and that belief hasn't changed.
evidence.source_title: JPMORGAN CHASE & CO earnings call 2026Q1 (quarter ended 2026-03-31)

evidence.snippet: On consumer, we talked about expecting low single-digit growth this year, that expectation is still in effect.
evidence.source_title: JPMORGAN CHASE & CO earnings call 2026Q2 (quarter ended 2026-06-30)

evidence.snippet: Maybe you see a little bit of additional outflow pressure, which results in slightly weaker deposit growth.
evidence.source_title: JPMORGAN CHASE & CO earnings call 2026Q3 (quarter ended 2026-09-30)

insights.title: AI agents and cyber risk become explicit concerns
insights.summary: In the Q1 2026 call Jamie Dimon said AI had made cyber risk worse and harder and that cyber was the firm's largest risk. In the Q3 call he cited rogue AI agents as a defensive concern, and management said the AI theme is broadly diffused across the marketplace, including in lending exposures.
insights.uw_relevance: AI-driven cyber, fraud and third-party agent risk are new operational and liability exposures for the bank. Management said these risks are heightened and cannot be fully quantified, so underwriters would need to rely on qualitative disclosure.

evidence.snippet: AI has made cyber risk worse and harder; generative models create additional vulnerabilities.

followups.question: What portion of the $1,780.90B uninsured deposit balance could leave if higher rates drive outflows, and how is that exposure being tracked?
followups.summary: Uninsured deposits were 64.0% of total deposits at FY2026 Q3, up from 60.9% at FY2025 Q4, an estimated $1,780.90B. The Q3 call said higher rates could bring additional outflow pressure and weaker growth.
followups.uw_relevance: A rising uninsured share raises deposit-run and liquidity exposure that the 10-Q risk factors flag as company-specific.

followups.question: What is the current status of the Florida civil suit naming the bank and its CEO, and what claims does it allege against the individual?
followups.summary: A January 2026 civil suit in Florida state court names JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. and its CEO as defendants. The filings list it as open, in the Fair Access to Banking matter.
followups.uw_relevance: Naming the CEO personally in a high-profile matter bears directly on individual D&O exposure and reputational claims.

followups.question: Which private credit and leveraged positions show weaker covenants or rollover risk, and what has tightening changed in the roughly $50 billion private credit book?
followups.summary: The CFO put private credit exposure at about $50 billion within a $160 billion core NBFI exposure. The CEO said some credit terms had loosened, including weaker covenants, and that the firm is tightening credit.
followups.uw_relevance: Concentration in private and leveraged credit with reported underwriting softness is a credit risk to monitor in D&O review.

followups.question: Has the Senate Democratic investigation into historical Epstein ties formally opened, and what records or executive testimony could it request?
followups.summary: A news report says a Senate Democratic investigation into JPMorgan's historical banking ties with Jeffrey Epstein is planned. No opening of the probe is confirmed in the input.
followups.uw_relevance: The probe could extend to executive testimony and records requests, which bears on D&O exposure even though it is not yet confirmed.

followups.question: How will leadership be divided between Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh as Co-Presidents, and who succeeds Daniel Pinto as President and COO when he retires at the end of 2026?
followups.summary: Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh were elected Co-Presidents in June 2026. President and COO Daniel Pinto will retire at the end of 2026.
followups.uw_relevance: Leadership transitions at the top of the firm bear on management continuity and key-person exposure in D&O review.

followups.question: What capital deployment plan sits behind the fall in buybacks, and how much of the about $30 billion of excess capital is earmarked for organic growth or deals?
followups.summary: Share repurchases fell from $8.32B in FY2026 Q1 to $6.79B in Q2 and $1.11B in Q3. Management referred to about $30 billion of excess capital in the Q3 call.
followups.uw_relevance: A sharp shift in capital return that management ties to investment priorities is relevant to shareholder-facing disclosure review.

followups.question: What did the US investigation find about WePay account closures, and what remediation has been completed since the subsidiary was shut down?
followups.summary: A US investigation found that WePay, a JPMorgan subsidiary, discriminated against conservative customers by closing accounts. JPMorgan said WePay has been shut down and that its policies prohibit discrimination.
followups.uw_relevance: Possible customer-discrimination claims or regulatory follow-up could arise even though the company says the subsidiary is shut down.

followups.question: What is the expected timing and potential financial outcome of the EURIBOR appeal, the India fine appeal and the South Africa Competition Tribunal matter?
followups.summary: The Firm is appealing the European Commission EURIBOR antitrust decision and a 2021 India Enforcement Directorate fine of about $31.5M. A South Africa Competition Commission FX matter is pending before the Competition Tribunal.
followups.uw_relevance: Several unresolved foreign enforcement matters with pending appeals bear on regulatory-investigation exposure in D&O review.

followups.question: What is the expected impact on credit provisions and portfolio risk from the Apple Card transaction before the closing about 24 months after the forward purchase commitment?
followups.summary: Chase will become the new issuer of Apple Card, following a forward purchase commitment dated December 30, 2025. A footnote ties $2.2 billion of provision for credit losses to the transaction, with closing expected about 24 months later.
followups.uw_relevance: A large portfolio acquisition with a long closing timeline bears on integration and credit-portfolio risk.

followups.question: How is the firm measuring AI-driven cyber, fraud and rogue agent risk, and what controls cover third-party AI agents?
followups.summary: In the Q1 2026 call Jamie Dimon said AI had made cyber risk worse and that cyber was the firm's largest risk. In the Q3 call he cited rogue AI agents as a defensive concern.
followups.uw_relevance: AI-driven cyber and third-party agent risk are new operational and liability exposures that management says cannot be fully quantified.

followups.question: What fee lines have slowed since the Q3 call said market conditions had recently reduced activity, and how much of the investment banking pipeline is at risk?
followups.summary: In the Q3 call management said evolving market conditions had recently slowed activity, and IB fees were up 14%. Total revenue growth year on year fell from 27.7% in FY2026 Q2 to 8.1% in Q3.
followups.uw_relevance: Fee income in investment banking is the most cyclical part of revenue, so a pipeline slowdown bears on near-term earnings and reporting.

followups.question: How much of the $4.6 billion Visa gain is in reported FY2026 Q2 results, and how do net income comparisons look excluding it?
followups.summary: The exchange produced a net gain of $4.6 billion in Corporate, and all Visa C shares were sold by September 30, 2026. Reported net income was $21.16B in FY2026 Q2, against $15.30B in Q3.
followups.uw_relevance: A one-time gain affects reported earnings comparisons across the 2026 quarters, which bears on the reliability of period results.

followups.question: How is the 1.8% allowance ratio reconciled with the reported loosening of credit terms, and is the nonperforming loan ratio trend changing?
followups.summary: Allowance for loan losses stayed at 1.8% of loans from FY2026 Q1 to Q3, and the nonperforming loan ratio was 0.7% at FY2025 Q4.
followups.uw_relevance: Reported credit ratios show no deterioration yet, a mitigating point against the qualitative loosening of underwriting noted elsewhere.

followups.question: How is the liquidity buffer tracking as uninsured deposits rise, and how has the Liquidity Coverage Ratio moved across recent quarters?
followups.summary: Liquidity Coverage Ratio was 113.0% at FY2026 Q3, and total deposits rose 9.1% year on year to $2,780.79B.
followups.uw_relevance: Liquidity buffers are a mitigating point, though the rising uninsured share in the same period tempers them.

metric_relevance.buyback_intensity: Buybacks equaled 0.07x net income in FY2026 Q3, against 0.63x in FY2025 Q4, a sharp change in capital returns after a steady run of ratios between 0.50x and 0.63x through FY2025.
metric_relevance.buybacks: Share repurchases dropped to $1.11B in FY2026 Q3 from $6.79B in Q2 and $8.32B in Q1, after $31.59B in FY2025. The CEO attributed the cut to redeploying capital, which underwriters can test against the capital ratios and the stated focus on organic growth.
metric_relevance.cet1_ratio: The standardized CET1 ratio fell to 14.0% at FY2026 Q3 from 14.8% a year earlier and 15.7% at FY2024 year-end, which makes capital headroom the central question. The Q3 call cited 13.9% for the same quarter-end, and the table value does not match it.
metric_relevance.deposit_growth_yoy: Deposits grew 9.1% year on year in FY2026 Q3, up from 6.4% at FY2025 year-end and 0.2% at FY2024 year-end. The Q3 call reported consumer deposit growth of 4% but flagged possible outflow pressure from higher rates.
metric_relevance.deposits: Total deposits reached $2,780.79B at FY2026 Q3, up from $2,559.32B at FY2025 year-end, and the uninsured share of that base is the liquidity question. Outflow risk from higher-yielding products sits against the growth.
metric_relevance.equity: Stockholders' equity grew to $372.37B in FY2026 Q3 from $362.44B at FY2025 year-end, yet the CET1 ratio fell over the same period, so the equity base alone does not show capital headroom.
metric_relevance.fee_income_growth_yoy: Fee income growth slowed to 3.0% year on year in FY2026 Q3 from 46.7% in FY2026 Q2, and FY2025 growth was 2.4%. The Q3 call's IB fee growth of 14% and its description of slowed activity are the context for this decline.
metric_relevance.lcr: The Liquidity Coverage Ratio was 113.0% at FY2026 Q3, within a range of 110.0% to 113.0% across the quarters shown. With uninsured deposits rising, the buffer is the key liquidity check.
metric_relevance.loan_loss_reserve_ratio: The allowance held at 1.8% of loans from FY2026 Q1 to Q3, below the 1.9% level of FY2024 Q4 and FY2025 Q1 to Q3, even as the Q3 call described looser credit terms. Whether reserves reflect private credit terms is the test of this ratio.
metric_relevance.net_income: Net income was $15.30B in FY2026 Q3, down from $21.16B in FY2026 Q2, and FY2025 net income of $57.05B was below FY2024's $58.47B. Whether the $4.6B Visa share exchange gain sits in the Q2 figure determines how much of the drop is underlying.
metric_relevance.nim: Net interest margin was 2.5% in FY2026 Q3, against 2.4% in FY2026 Q2 and 2.6% in FY2024, and deposit pricing is the main pressure. The Q3 call warned that higher rates could bring outflow pressure and weaker deposit growth.
metric_relevance.noninterest_income: Noninterest income was $23.14B in FY2026 Q3, down from $31.84B in FY2026 Q2, against $87.00B for FY2025. Investment banking fees drive much of this line, and the Q3 call said activity had slowed.
metric_relevance.npl_ratio: The nonperforming loan ratio was 0.7% at FY2025 Q4, up from 0.5% at FY2023 year-end, though it was 1.0% at FY2020 year-end. A rise in NPLs alongside looser credit terms would signal weaker credit quality.
metric_relevance.revenue: Total revenue was $57.35B in FY2026 Q2 and $50.17B in FY2026 Q3, and the Q2 level sits alongside the $4.6B Visa share exchange gain, so the Q2 base needs adjusting before quarters are compared. FY2025 revenue totaled $182.45B.
metric_relevance.revenue_growth_qoq: Quarter-on-quarter growth swung from 15.1% in FY2026 Q2 to -12.5% in FY2026 Q3, a reversal large enough that the Q2 peak must be adjusted before the Q3 decline is read as a trend.
metric_relevance.revenue_growth_yoy: Year-on-year revenue growth was 27.7% in FY2026 Q2 and 8.1% in FY2026 Q3, against 2.8% for FY2025 as a whole. The Q3 call said investment banking activity had slowed and IB fees rose 14%, which is the main near-term check on whether growth holds.
metric_relevance.roa: Return on average assets was 1.4% in FY2025, down from 1.5% in FY2024 and 1.0% in FY2022. The FY2025 decline follows net income falling from $58.47B to $57.05B.
metric_relevance.roe: Return on average equity was 16.1% in FY2025, down from 17.4% in FY2024, while equity rose to $362.44B at FY2025 year-end. Lower returns on a growing equity base sharpen questions about how capital is being deployed.
metric_relevance.tier1_ratio: The Tier 1 capital ratio fell to 14.9% at FY2026 Q3 from 15.5% at FY2025 year-end and 16.8% at FY2024 year-end, declining in every quarter shown since FY2024 Q4. This trend runs in the same direction as the CET1 decline.
metric_relevance.uninsured_deposit_share: Uninsured deposits reached 64.0% of total deposits at FY2026 Q3, up from 60.9% at FY2025 year-end and 56.1% at FY2023 year-end. The 10-Q risk factors name loss of deposits to higher-yielding products as a liquidity risk.
metric_relevance.unrealized_loss_to_equity: Unrealized securities losses were 6.9% of equity at FY2026 Q3, up from 4.7% at FY2025 year-end, so the securities book takes a larger share of the equity base. This affects how capital looks when securities values move.
